statement: Transition history contains predictive information about the next state beyond the current state.
motivation: Charter §37: if computation is 'about transitions', history should matter.
assumptions: plug-in entropy estimates at N=200000 are accurate to ~1e-4 bit
predictions: If universal: I(X_{t+1}; X_{t-1} | X_t) > 0 for every source.
falsification: CMI below 10x Miller-Madow bias for some source (a counterexample to the universal form).

revision_history.note: Universal form disproven: EXP-B measured CMI 1.7e-05 (iid) and 9.9e-06 (state-Markov) bits, below 10x bias bound 2.5e-04, i.e. no predictive information from history beyond x_t; CMI 0.365 bits for the transition-Markov source. By DRV-006 the property is exactly 'the process is not first-order Markov in this representation' — collapses to established theory (Markov order). Not a property of computation in general.

statement: Representing a computation by its transitions rather than its states exposes structure that the state representation hides.
assumptions: 'structure' must be made measurable: information content, Markov order, compressibility
predictions: information-content form: transitions carry information not in states
model-order form: Markov order differs between representations
falsification: information-content form falsified if the recoding is information-preserving up to a constant; model-order form falsified if Markov orders coincide for all tested sources.

revision_history.note: Information-content form disproven: the XOR transition recoding of a binary sequence has fibers {x, complement(x)} (EXP-F: 512 fibers of size 2 on {0,1}^10), loses exactly 1 bit, and is lossless given x_0. Transitions carry no information absent from states. The model-order form (what changes is the distribution of memory over time) continues as H-012; see INT-001.

statement: Computation admits a natural seven-stage stratification: State, Transition, Temporal History, Transition Topology, Computational Structure, Representation, Meta-Substrate.
assumptions: 'natural' must be operationalised, e.g. as boundaries where projections stop being congruences, or where new measurable quantities appear
predictions: an operational criterion applied to real systems yields seven levels, in this order
falsification: an operational layer criterion yields a different count/order, or the levels are shown to be orthogonal dimensions rather than a sequence.

revision_history.note: No test performed. Interpretation INT-004 (non-monotone distance across layers) and EXP-F (projection axis independent of time axis) argue against a single linear hierarchy, but interpretations cannot change status. Operational test queued as Q-006.

statement: In deterministic dynamics, exact masking or recovery of a state perturbation requires the dynamics to be non-injective (information-losing).
motivation: Links perturbation attenuation (§34) to information loss (§16).
predictions: no masked/recovered outcome under injective rules (EXP-D)
falsification: a masked/recovered outcome under an injective rule.

revision_history.note: DRV-001 proves necessity. EXP-D corroborates: 0 masked/recovered outcomes in 192 trials for each injective rule (51, 150, 170, 204 on the 16-ring); masking present for rules 0, 90, 110, 232. Non-injectivity is NOT sufficient: rules 30 and 184 are non-injective with 0/192 masked. Rule 90 recovery at exactly k=8 matches DRV-002.

statement: In the simulated layered model, a single-bit storage perturbation under a distance-3 code is attenuated to zero at the architectural layer; under parity it becomes a detection event; unprotected it always reaches the architectural layer.
assumptions: single-error fault model; flip present at read time
falsification: any SDC from a single present flip under hamming/secded; any undetected single flip under parity.

revision_history.note: EXP-G (reproduced): hamming and secded corrected 100% of single flips present at read; parity detected 100% (DUE); unprotected propagated 100% to L1. Scope: the simulated model only. No statement about physical memories.

statement: The minimum information that must survive between two representations is not a single quantity: it depends on the property to be preserved.
assumptions: 'property' = an observable O whose entire future must be predictable
predictions: coarsest congruence sizes differ across observables for the same dynamics (EXP-F F6)
falsification: coarsest congruence size independent of the observable for every tested dynamics.

revision_history.note: Collapses to established theory: the minimum retained information for an observable O is the coarsest congruence refining ker O (Moore minimisation / bisimulation quotient). EXP-F: for increment on 8 bits the minimum is 2 states (O=bit0), 16 (low4), 256 (msb/threshold/parity/popcount); for eca90, 2 (parity) to 256. The charter's boxed question has a precise answer relative to O and no answer without O.

statement: The Computational Transition Graph (CTG) is a mathematical object distinct from established transition systems / graphs.
predictions: some CTG attribute is required by an experiment and not expressible as an annotated LTS
falsification: not falsifiable by one experiment; evaluated by accumulated mapping.

revision_history.note: INT-002: every CTG attribute used so far is expressible as an annotated LTS/functional graph. Absence of a distinct object is not disproof; CTG is kept as an internal alias (C-009, PROVISIONAL).

statement: Structural lifting (structures becoming states of a higher-level system) yields new measurable information at each level, rather than collapsing into an established formalism or becoming redundant.
predictions: a lifted system (e.g. functional graphs under rewires) has attractors/transients not predictable from level-0 statistics
falsification: lifted-level measurements are functions of level-0 measurements.

statement: The structural effect of rewiring one edge of a functional graph is bounded by the ancestor set of the rewired vertex and is dominated by rewires of cyclic vertices.
motivation: Structural perturbation (§25) needs a predictor of effect size.
predictions: on-cycle mean effect >> off-cycle mean effect
falsification: bound violated; or off-cycle effects comparable to on-cycle effects.

revision_history.note: Bound part: DERIVED (DRV-003); never violated in 1280 rewires. Dominance part: on-cycle vs off-cycle mean fraction of states whose attractor changed = 0.70 vs 0.006 (eca30), 0.76 vs 0.032 (random map), 1.0 vs 0.0014 (eca90). The prediction had no numeric threshold (F-007), so it cannot be EXPERIMENTALLY_SUPPORTED; status SIMULATED.

statement: Detecting an inconsistency does not identify its cause: an error-correcting decoder's inferred error location is correct only under its assumed fault model.
predictions: location correct for 100% of single flips, 0% of double flips (G5, G6)
falsification: decoder location correct for any double flip.

revision_history.note: DRV-005 plus EXP-G: Hamming(7,4) inferred location correct for 5040/5040 corrected single flips and 0/3360 double flips (all miscorrected -> SDC). SECDED detects all 4480 double flips but reports no location. Detection reports an inconsistency relative to a fault model; it does not identify a cause.

statement: Normalised perturbation distance need not be monotone across abstraction layers: amplification at one layer can coexist with attenuation at the next.
motivation: Charter §33-34: 'larger' must be defined per layer.
assumptions: distances normalised per layer as in substrate/layers.py
predictions: G7: some unprotected injections grow L1->L2 and shrink L2->L3
falsification: no such injection exists in the exhaustive campaign.

revision_history.note: Pre-registered G7 passed and reproduced: 1413 of 2880 unprotected single flips present at read have normalised distance increasing L1->L2 and decreasing L2->L3. Scope: this simulated model and these normalisations (OP-006 questions the normalisation itself).

statement: There exist binary processes whose finite Markov order is strictly lower in the XOR-transition representation than in the state representation.
predictions: B4: CMI in state space > 10x bias; B5: CMI in transition space < 10x bias, for the transition-Markov source

revision_history.note: State-space CMI 0.365 bits vs transition-space CMI 5.6e-06 bits (bias bound 2.5e-04). Pre-registered B4/B5 passed; reproduced. The converse direction (order increases under recoding) is post-hoc: DISC-001.

statement: The fraction of storage perturbations that are logically masked is a property of the (program, output observable) pair, not of the storage perturbation alone.
motivation: EXP-G first execution showed 0% logical masking with a checksum output (F-003).
predictions: masking fraction differs across output observables

revision_history.note: Unprotected single flips present at read: masked 0% (full output or checksum), 80.0% (max), 93.7% (alarm). Post-hoc, so capped at SIMULATED; rediscovers ACE/AVF reasoning (LIT-011).

statement: The research process itself can be represented with the laboratory's transition-graph machinery: the identifier-level provenance graph of the research loop contains cycles, while the versioned (revision-level) graph is acyclic, as a transition system and its unrolled trace are.
predictions: versioned graph is a DAG; collapsed graph has >=1 nontrivial SCC once a hypothesis is revised from evidence of an experiment testing it
falsification: versioned graph cyclic, or collapsed graph acyclic after revisions.

revision_history.note: Prediction written into the registry before regenerating the graph; confirmed (4 SCCs collapsed, DAG versioned). Largely by construction; its practical value is that tools/validate.py uses the versioned DAG property as an integrity check.
